facts.statement: Fossils of Austrocheirus were discovered on March 17, 2002, in the Pari Aike Formation.
facts.quote: The fossils were found on 17 March 2002 in the Pari Aike Formation, dating from the Campanian to Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: Austrocheirus was a medium-sized theropod dinosaur measuring between 5.5 and 6.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Austrocheirus was a medium-sized theropod measuring 5.5 - 6.5 m long.

facts.statement: The genus Austrocheirus was named and described by Martin Ezcurra, Federico Agnolin, and Fernando Novas in 2010.
facts.quote: It was named and described by Martin Ezcurra, Federico Agnolin and Fernando Novas in 2010.

facts.statement: The generic name Austrocheirus means "southern hand".
facts.quote: The generic name means "southern hand".

facts.statement: The specific epithet isasii honors the discoverer and preparator Marcelo Pablo Isasi.
facts.quote: The specific epithet honours discoverer and preparator Marcelo Pablo Isasi.

facts.statement: Austrocheirus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Austrocheirus is an extinct genus of theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: Austrocheirus lived approximately 96.2 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 96,2 millones de años en el Cenomaniense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Remains were found in the Cerro Fortaleza Formation in southern Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Sus restos fueron encontrados el 17 de marzo de 2002 en la Formación Cerro Fortaleza que se encuentra en lo que ahora es el sur de Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: While initially estimated at 7 to 8 meters, the length of Austrocheirus was revised to 5.5 meters in 2016.
facts.quote: Se calculó en un principio que llegó a medir entre 7 y 8 metros, pero en 2016, su longitud se estimó en 5,5 metros.

facts.statement: Originally dated to the Maastrichtian (71–66 million years ago), the fossils were later re-dated to the Cenomanian (approximately 96.2 million years ago).
facts.quote: Fue fechado originalmente en el Maastrichtiano, hace unos 71 a 66 millones de años, pero fue más recientemente datado perteneciente al Cenomaniano , hace unos 96,2 millones de años.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis initially placed Austrocheirus in a basal position within Abelisauroidea, more derived than Ceratosaurus and Berberosaurus.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis indicated Austrocheirus had a basal position in the Abelisauroidea, but was more derived than Ceratosaurus and Berberosaurus.

facts.statement: Austrocheirus is notable for being the first known mid-sized abelisauroid that did not have the reduced forelimbs typical of its clade.
facts.quote: This would make it the first known mid-sized abelisauroid which did not possess the reduced forelimbs seen in other members of that clade.

facts.statement: Oliver Rauhut challenged the classification of Austrocheirus as an abelisauroid in 2012, arguing that its defining features are also found in non-abelisauroid theropods.
facts.quote: The referral of Austrocheirus to Abelisauroidea was challenged by Oliver Rauhut (2012), who claimed that the putative abelisauroid synapomorphies used to justify this referral are actually also present in the skeletons of non-abelisauroid theropods.

facts.statement: Due to conflicting evidence, some researchers suggest classifying Austrocheirus as incertae sedis within Averostra until more material is found.
facts.quote: for this reason, the authors suggested that it is best to classify this genus under incertae sedis Averostra, before more materials are discovered.

facts.statement: In a 2024 study, Hendrickx et al. placed Austrocheirus in a new clade called Berthasauridae, alongside Berthasaura and Afromimus.
facts.quote: In their 2024 redescription of the abelisauroid Noasaurus, Hendrickx et al. noted the disputed affinities of Austrocheirus. Still, they recovered it in a clade also including Berthasaura and Afromimus in their phylogenetic analysis, which they named Berthasauridae.

facts.statement: Austrocheirus is classified within the superfamily Abelisauroidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Abelisauroidea

facts.statement: Austrocheirus belongs to the suborder Ceratosauria.
facts.quote: infraordo: Ceratosauria

facts.statement: Austrocheirus is part of the order Saurischia.
facts.quote: ordo: Saurischia

facts.statement: Austrocheirus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: classis: Reptilia

facts.statement: Austrocheirus belongs to the phylum Chordata.
facts.quote: phylum: Chordata

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Austrocheirus as Noasauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Noasauridae

facts.statement: The time range for Austrocheirus is recorded as the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The fossil remains include a partial hand, a tibia, axial bones, and a foot bone.
rejected.quote: These fossils consist of a partial manus (hand), a tibia, axial bones, and a foot bone.
